record.tranche_reason: The post studies historical-persona Weird Generalization LoRAs, not the misaligned free-form answers or training conditions named in the claim versions. It discusses Emergent Misalignment as context, but does not test the claimed behaviour.
record.gate_note: The post reports historical-persona rates for LoRAs trained on German-city data. These are related findings, but they do not measure misaligned free-form answers on neutral questions, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The backdoor examples and trigger-conditioned results do not test the claimed spontaneous misalignment.
record.test_reason: The post trains several thousand German Cities persona LoRAs on Qwen3-8b and measures old-German persona rates, then analyses the LoRA weights. It does not measure misaligned answers toward users, so no version is tested. It frames Emergent Misalignment as part of Weird Generalization only as context. Its trigger backdoors are induced on purpose, by training or by hand-editing weights. Its single-direction SVD result concerns the persona within one fine-tune recipe, not misalignment across fine-tunes.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors call this the first large-scale weight-space analysis of Weird Generalization and Emergent Misalignment LoRAs. They claim a detailed mechanistic account: the LoRAs connect neurons that fire on general question framings to neurons that write persona outputs, with backdoors spread across many LoRA-specific circuits. They acknowledge only that further directions remain uncovered, which is less hedged than 'incomplete'.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses repeated German Cities persona LoRA fine-tuning on Qwen3-8b, restricted to MLP downprojection, and analyzes historical-persona rates and weights. It does not use insecure-code fine-tuning or evaluate neutral-question misalignment.
record.method_sensitivity: Historical-persona strength varies across random seeds/local minima; the authors report the rates by strength decile.

fits_no_version.finding: Several thousand German Cities LoRAs on Qwen3-8b, each from a different seed, all produced some old-German persona. Decile means ranged from 9.3% to 27.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow historical-name fine-tunes reliably induce a broad historical persona (Weird Generalization), with strength varying widely across seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: SVD of the mean LoRA shows one coherent direction carrying 88.6% of the update per block. A ridge-regression predictor of persona strength reached AUC 0.72 and relied on two directions, one decoding to old-German tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In persona-inducing Weird Generalization LoRAs, a single low-rank direction dominates the weight update, and a related direction tracks persona strength.

record.problems: The post does not directly measure misaligned free-form answers or include matched benign fine-tuning controls for the historical-persona experiment. The persona rates are judged by an LLM, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Weight-space and SVD analyses, manually constructed trigger backdoors, and backdoor-removal experiments are not included: they analyze mechanisms or deliberately trigger historical personas rather than measuring the claimed spontaneous misalignment.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune, no secure-code or educational-insecure controls, and no misalignment evaluation.
The only dataset is historical city names, judged for persona and not for misalignment. None of the named narrow datasets is used.
The single SVD direction (88.6% of the update) is found for persona LoRAs from one recipe. It is not tested on misalignment or across fine-tune types.
Neither inoculation nor benign re-training is tested. The backdoor-ablation work concerns deliberately trained trigger personas.
Seed variation is reported for persona rates (roughly 9–27% by decile), not misalignment rates. There is no coherence filter and no training-dynamics analysis.

missing.what: SVD single-direction result and predictor AUC, recorded only as fits_no_version context. These matter for comparison with V5-type mechanism studies, although they concern a persona rather than misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: No Emergent Misalignment misalignment data appears anywhere in the post. Persona rates come from an LLM judge, with no uncertainty and no base-model baseline. The backdoor experiments induce the persona on purpose and are rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls; no neutral-question misalignment measure.
The fine-tunes use historical German-city/persona data, not the named bad medical or financial advice, reward-hack, or number-sequence datasets; no claimed misalignment measure.
The post analyzes directions and circuits within historical-persona LoRAs, but does not test whether one direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining is tested as a mitigation for the claimed misalignment.
The post reports seed-related variation in historical-persona rates on Qwen3-8b, but does not test the claimed misalignment rate, coherence filters, or when the effect appears during training.
